recipes.name: Quick and Easy Apple Muffins
ingredients_raw: 1 cup apple - peeled, cored, and chopped

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease 12 muffin cups or line with paper muffin liners.

Stir together flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. Stir together milk, egg, and butter in a separate bowl. Stir egg mixture into flour mixture just until combined. Fold in chopped apples. Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center of muffins comes out clean, 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick and Easy Apple Muffins
raw_recipe.description: A tasty, easy apple muffins recipe spiced with cinnamon that make a great breakfast treat. These are simple and quick to make in just 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I see a lot of people who say this recipe is bland. One reason for that is it is supposed to be a diabetic recipe. So for all the non-diabetics, adding more sugar may improve the flavour. I have also seen some reviews that they were chewy or tough - that means you are over-mixing the batter. Remember- muffin batter is only mixed until just combined. Just some hints I thought may help.

I absolutely love this! I added two teaspoons of extra cinnamon and added a teaspoon of pumpkin spice. Then I chopped 4 green apples and stirred them in cinnamon sugar. I also substituted butter with applesauce. I will definitely make this again.

Thank you for all the good reviews. I usually make a recipe as written the first time before changing anything, but due to the helpful reviews I tweaked this one a bit. Some reviews say that they didn't rise enough, so I put 3 tsp. baking powder instead of just 2, used half white and half whole wheat flour and they rose just right. I put 1 tsp cinnamon, instead of 1/2 and used 1-1/4 c. milk, instead 1 cup. I used 2 med.-large apples which came out to be 1-1/2 to 2 cups of chopped apple instead of just one cup. The salt and sugar content were perfect for me. I'm trying to cut back on sugar and I like the taste better. Most muffins are more overly sweet nowadays than they used to be. They're muffins, not cake. I like butter on mine and they are delicious, easy and cheap to make.

I just made these muffins and they turned out great! I used a cup of whole wheat flour and a cup of white all purpose flour. I also added 1/4 cup of brown sugar. I like my apples mixed in good. So I cooked my chopped apples on the stove with a little bit of apple juice. Then processed them in the food processor and folded them in! they turn out perfect.

I made these for my godfather who is a diabetic, and based on these reviews I wanted to make it sweeter. I changed the milk to a can of apple juice concentrate, added 1/2 cup of raisins to the dry ingredients, 1/2 tsp of ginger and two packets of sugar substitute. I mashed a banana into the wet as well and they are pretty delicious-thanks for the recipe ideas!
p.s. I totally agree with the pp, you have to almost leave muffins not quite blended, so they rise and aren't tough.

It's actually a great recipe if you don't mind playing around with ingredients! I added 1/4 cup of brown sugar, and threw in a leftover package of Quaker oats (maple flavour). I also put less salt (1/4 teaspoon), and a bit more cinnamon. I also made sure to mix the dry and wet ingredients separately first.
The recipe was very thick. I added another cup of milk. Muffins were very light and fluffy. They were bland though. I would add another apple, more cinnamon and vanilla the next time I try them.

Because of other reviews saying it was bland. I substituted white sugar for brown sugar. I added 2 teaspoon vanilla extract, 2tablespoons of lemon juiceand increased the milk to 21/2 cups. (Didn't want the muffins dry). I loved them with the changes. I gave this a three star because I had to make so many changes. I alao put a little sugar on the apples as one reviewer suggested. Great idea! My husband and I devoured these muffins. He requested I make more today.

After reading these were bland I made the following changes: 1. I doubled the sugar, 2. used 1/2 c milk and 1/2 c orange juice, 3. added grated lemon peel, 4. doubled the apple, 5. and substituted 1/2 c instant vanilla pudding mix for 1/2 c flour. I also had to add a little extra milk because the batter was too stiff. I ended up with one very large, flavorful loaf of bread. I also cooked them at 325 for 35 minutes so they wouldn't get burnt on the outside.

These turned out very good. I did add a small amount of extra sugar. I had a bag of fresh cranberries that I had boiled with a small amount of water and sugar and had cooled in the fridge overnight and I added some of these to the batter, along with one large chopped apple. The batter seemed a little thin, but they turned out perfect!

After reading the reviews I decided to add some extra flavour. I made the following changes: 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 grated apple, 3/4cups brown sugar, 1 cup wholewheat flour with 1 cup white flour,zest of 1 orange and then chopped up and added the flesh of the orange (after removing pith). It was really delicious but not too sweet and the orange provided little pops of moisture that worked well.

You’re absolutely correct, overmixing causes dense and overmoist muffin baking. When adding ingredients I put in 1cup of sugar (instead of 1/2 C, without having read the comments. Depending on the apple goods you’re making, I find that macintosh apples give off a lot of flavor and gets more involved in the whole product (softer and jucier than the usual “grannie smith” standby. Also using more spices enhances the flavor like allspice, extra cinnamon, nutmeg and maybe just a bit of turmeric (1/4 teaspoon) Otherwise, great recipe. Remember, don’t over mix! And possibly sprinkle regular sugar over each muffin after you fill your muffin tins for an additional bit of texture

These are just ok. A little spongy for my taste. I like my muffins more crumbly. I DID NOT over work the dough. Following others recommendations, I put in 1/3 c. sugar, added an extra teaspoon of cinnamon and added a 1/4 c. apple cider. I also added 1/2 c. chopped pecans for extra crunch.

I substituted sour cream for milk although normally I sour the milk which added a softness to batter. Also used maple syrup instead of sugar and oil instead of butter. Oh and also used a combo of GF and coconut flour instead of regular flour. Used the receipt as a guide. They were delicious!!
Super easy to make. Tasted good, but bland. I would recommend adding more cinnamon for a bit more flavor.
Muffins turned out really tough, not moist at all. I even added a bit of applesauce and more sugar but still very bland. Did not rise much either. Recipe fail
They turned out delicious.I made a double batch.And I added a cup of sugar.Thank you very much for sharing:)

I made the recipe as is and it was super quick and easy (which was what I needed ahah), and so delicious, I will make it again! There are two muffins missing on the picture because we test tasted them of course!!
Sad but they turned out like lead balls We laughed but they were horrible. nothing was missed. Very disappointing
